label: early-mid original-phase first occurrence of n/j/u/h/k/p/1/2 after t/y/v/s/k/w context
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (98% of mass), at positions t=2..8, peaking at t=3-5. It never fires at t=0-1 or anywhere in the copy phase; on the delimiter step it fires only weakly (2% of mass). Whether it fires depends on two things together. (1) The current input: n is by far the strongest (8x lift, 31% of mass), then j, u, h, 1, 2, k, p, and it is usually the first occurrence of that token (94% of mass). (2) The tokens already seen: activation is much more likely when t, y (strongest), v, s, k or w appeared earlier, e.g. as the first token or two steps back. The top activations are sequences that start with y t and then have n. The current-token set alone has 88% recall but only 9% precision, and adding the context condition caps precision near 35-50%. This suggests a graded, roughly additive readout of the current token plus the prefix composition, not a clean boolean rule. Magnitude is highest when n follows an early y/t context. Dev F1 is about 0.39 and mass recall about 0.54.
